hints: Think about the size of each airway in order: trachea to bronchi to bronchioles. Which ones are wide tubes that must be held open all the time?
Remember the job of cartilage is rigid support to prevent collapse, while bronchioles need smooth muscle to constrict and control airflow, not rigid cartilage.
walkthrough:
**Recall the job of cartilage**

Think of cartilage as a stiff support ring. It keeps large airways open so air can flow freely in and out, even when pressure changes during breathing.

**Map cartilage along the airways**

The trachea has C-shaped rings of cartilage. The bronchi (the two large branches into the lungs) also have plates of cartilage to hold them open. This is always true in a healthy human.

**Check the bronchioles**

Bronchioles are much smaller and have no cartilage at all. Instead their walls have lots of smooth muscle so they can narrow or widen to control air distribution. So any option that includes bronchioles must be wrong.

options.A: Partly right but incomplete. Cartilage is in the trachea, but it is also always in the bronchi, so 'only' makes this false.
options.B: Partly right but incomplete. Cartilage is in the bronchi, but it is also always in the trachea, so 'only' makes this false.
options.C: Incorrect because bronchioles never contain cartilage. They have smooth muscle for constriction instead of rigid support.
options.D: Correct. Both the trachea and the bronchi always have cartilage to support the airway wall and prevent collapse during ventilation.
